newsitem.title: CHINA: Hang Seng Bank sees rosy second half.
newsitem.headline: Hang Seng Bank sees rosy second half.

text.p: Hang Seng Bank Ltd, a subsidiary of HSBC Holdings Plc, posted a healthy 14.5 percent rise in interim profits on Monday, and held out hopes that the rest of 1997 would be rosy on the back of a buoyant economy, its top officials said.

"In the second half of the year, export growth should rebound on the back of improved demand in the major markets and the relative stability of the Hong Kong dollar," said chairman Lee Quo-wei at a news conference.
"With further improvement in the employment market, consumer spending should maintain its growth momentum," he said.

For the first six months of 1997, profit attributable to shareholders rose to HK$4.98 billion compared with HK$4.35 billion in the same 1996 period. Analysts had expected net profit growth of between 11 and 15 percent.

The bank, which attributed its strong first half performance to a sustained growth in consumer spending and a buoyant local property market, also saw its operating profit rise 13.7 percent to HK$5.10 billion.

But it suffered a fall in residential mortgage pricing because of fierce competition. Its net interest margin for the first half of the year fell to 3.08 percent from 3.12 percent during the same period last year.
But it remained optimistic about the territory's property market. "The demand for loans has been very good and we did not need to go chasing to keep our market share," Lee said.

Advances to customers recorded strong growth of 18.2 percent, at HK$192.2 billion, compared with the end of 1996. "The strong growth was recorded mainly in corporate lending, residential mortgages," said vice-chairman Alexander Au.
In the longer term, the bank will focus on expanding its business in mainland China, the officials said.
"Confident of the potential on the mainland, we are putting more resources there as well as Hong Kong," Au said.
The bank, which has just received approval to open a branch in Shanghai, has one other branch in Guangzhou, Guangdong province.
